prompt: Count the four confusion-matrix outcomes for a binary classifier and derive accuracy and precision, with sensible fallbacks when a denominator is zero. Complete the ConfusionMatrix class in the starter file.
explanation: Every prediction falls into exactly one of four buckets, so a single pass over the two arrays with an if / else-if chain fills the whole matrix. Accuracy asks what fraction of all predictions were right; precision asks the narrower question of how many flagged positives really were positive, which is why a model that flags nothing has an undefined precision that we report as 0.0. Casting one operand to double before dividing is essential -- integer division would collapse 3/4 to 0.
hints: Count once in the constructor and store the four totals; the getters just return fields.
Four mutually exclusive cases fit an if / else if / else if / else chain over actual[i] and predicted[i].
Guard the divisions: accuracy returns 0.0 when total() is 0, and precision returns 0.0 when tp + fp is 0. Remember the (double) cast.
